en.title: Merge Three Sorted Arrays and Remove Duplicates
en.description:
Merge three non-decreasing integer arrays into one strictly increasing array, keeping each value only once. Input arrays may be empty.

The input format, examples, and test data were compiled and written by CSWork.
en.input: This site's standard input scale: first n m k (each 0..100000); the next three lines are the three arrays (an empty array is an empty line), with values in −10⁹..10⁹, and each array is non-decreasing.
en.output: Output the answer as described; separate multiple results with spaces in order, and output an empty line for an empty array.
en.explanation: Example 1: the distinct values across the three arrays are 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6; each is output once, in ascending order.
hints: Maintain three pointers; each time, take the smallest value not yet consumed, append it only if it differs from the last output, and then advance the pointer(s) that supplied this value.
